customManagers.description: Hugo builds the blog in the Dockerfile's builder stage from gohugoio's own release tarball, which no built-in datasource can see -- without this it would be the one dependency in the repo that rots silently.

packageRules.description: The nginx base image is the only dependency that reaches users, so its bump has to cut a release: commit it as fix: and release-please opens a release PR, the tag triggers publish.yml, and Renovate in the gitops repo rolls the new tag out. Held only 1 day rather than the repo-wide 5, because a base-image rebuild IS the security fix -- publish.yml fails a release on any HIGH/CRITICAL Grype finding, which is exactly what a stale base causes.
GitHub Actions updates never reach the image: commit as chore: so release-please records them in the changelog without cutting a release.
Auto-merge low-risk leaf-dependency updates (patch, minor, digest) once required checks are green -- matches dackota/change-tracking-dashboard's convention.
Never auto-merge a major bump; always leave it as a manual PR.

Hugo, last so it wins: later packageRules override earlier ones, and the patch/minor automerge rule above would otherwise re-enable auto-merge for it. Renovate can bump HUGO_VERSION but cannot compute the tarball checksums, so HUGO_SHA256_AMD64 and HUGO_SHA256_ARM64 must be updated by hand in the PR -- until they are, the image build fails on `sha256sum -c`, which is the intended loud failure rather than a silent unverified download. Committed as fix: because a Hugo bump changes the HTML that reaches readers, so it has to cut a release.
